figures_read.caption: After-minus-before differences for every metric, each with its 95% interval. The three panels carry three different scales, because a rate difference of 0.17 and a token difference of eleven million cannot share an axis without hiding the rates.

findings.summary: The 'failed or aborted requests' interval spans about 0.0031 of the top panel's 50-percentage-point range, so in the rendered PNG it is a roughly 6 px grey sliver from x 776 to x 784 straddling the zero line at x=778, and its estimate dot sits inside its own bar in the same colour: a reader can see that this row is essentially zero, but cannot read the interval's width or which way it leans, and has to take both from the document table (+0.0008 percentage points, -0.0007 to +0.0023). On a panel shared with a +17 pp and a -12 pp effect no honest linear scale can show that interval, so the shared scale is the right form and this is a limit of it rather than a defect to repair in the drawing; disposition: exempted, because a broken axis or an inset would overstate a 0.003-of-range interval and the table already carries the exact numbers.

item_verdicts.contrast: PASS — row and tick labels are near-black and the bottom note is mid grey (#555555), all on pure white, and no glyph is drawn over a bar or a fill, so every text element clears the contrast of its background by a wide margin.
item_verdicts.data_ink: PASS — the ink is twelve thin interval bars with end caps, twelve small dots and three thin vertical zero lines on white; no area encoding, no second redundant encoding and nothing decorative, so the intervals carry essentially all of the ink.
item_verdicts.decoration: PASS — no gradient, panel fill, background band, shadow or styled theme; the canvas is white with three bottom axis lines, three thin zero reference lines and the labels.
item_verdicts.label_collision: PASS — no label is clipped or overlapping: the ink bounding box is x 4-1396, y 3-875 of the 1400x881 canvas, so the longest row label ('failed or aborted requests', beginning at x=13) clears the left edge and the bottom note's last ink row is 875 with five rows of white beneath it; the three axis labels sit in the gaps at y≈269, 553 and 828 with the next panel's row labels starting at y≈323 and 611, and the marks that sit on a zero line are drawn above it (the grey bars cover x 777-786 at y=39 and y=185 over the #444444 line at x=778), so no mark is hidden by its reference line.
item_verdicts.legibility: PASS — the rendered PNG now carries its full text layer: three panel axis labels, twelve row labels, every tick label and the bottom note all render as solid glyph paths, each row label reading cleanly at about 14 pt, so a reader can name every metric and read each panel's scale at a glance.
item_verdicts.table_form: PASS — an interval plot of twelve per-metric differences on three scales shows the uncertainty that the document's §6 table reports only as bracketed numbers; this is geometry the table cannot carry, not information that belongs in one.
